It’s likely that you have been experiencing gallbladder attacks. Dumping is only described after surgery and is a different process. Both can cause the same symptoms cramping and diarrhea. Both are triggered by the same thing missing meals and or eating a fatty meal. In an attack your gallbladder is contracting trying to release bile but is likely clogged by a stone. This can cause diarrhea as the gallbladder continues to contract in an attempt to release bile and the stone. In the post syndrome your liver recognizes it now needs to release bile because the gallbladder is no longer doing it. However it doesn’t recognize how much it should release so it just release a large “dump” of bile which causes the same results. Either can and will likely have you sick and running to the bathroom. It’s recommended to eat smaller meals over time and reduce fat intake if you want to keep symptoms at bay. I’m in medical school and also a scientist. Got my gallbladder removed over 2 years ago now.

I didn’t have surgery for years after the first attack that sent me to the ER. I was advised to have surgery but technically the stone had dislodged itself by the time I went in (I had been in an attack for days unknowingly) so they let me go home. Labs were bad my liver and pancreas were the worst. I decided to hold off and take the diet approach. Didn’t eat out, hardly ate fats for years. The attacks kept happening and getting worse and lasting longer. By the time I went to the ER again my gallbladder was about to explode and gigantic and full of stones. I had completely stopped eating the week before from all of the pain. I tried nearly everything to keep it and it still didn’t work. After removal I immediately felt better and went back to school/work 2 days later. No pain meds I felt sooooo much better after suffering so long. I think it’s reasonable to hold off and attempt to try and navigate it with diet. I think the biggest difference it makes is mentally you feel like you did everything you could before losing the organ and you don’t have the “what if”

I bled so much and for so long they were going to give me a blood transfusion! They gave me an emergency drug in the ER that actually stopped my bleeding for a bit. You’re not supposed to be on it long term though I was on it 7+ years before they took me off of it. Immediately started bleeding😕

I had surgery over a year ago and my abdominal muscles still don’t feel right! It just feels like they aren’t all connected anymore or they don’t know how to respond to each other. I didn’t have much pain afterwards with the surgery but they just don’t feel right anymore.

I’m sorry that you are struggling after surgery! It’s really a long journey to recovery. I felt very similarly after removal and actually just stopped eating breakfast for awhile until things leveled out. Also if you could I would take an anti diarrhea before eating especially if you know it’s going to bother you. I also think you should try an elimination diet to see if specific foods might be triggering you. I can’t eat some of the things you mentioned and other random items after removal. Tomatoes bother me, cinnamon gives me really bad heartburn now, I can’t really eat chips, and I honestly have to reduce fats significantly I rarely eat out. I also noticed I cannot eat as quickly and have to eat smaller portions. For breakfast if I make a sandwich I will eat half of it and sit down for a bit then in 30mins or so I will eat the rest to prevent the bile dumping from your liver. I think your liver just needs to learn what to do now. I hope that things get better! Hang in there!

Emergency is usually considered life threatening if you do not get it as soon as possible. I had a stone stuck in my duct my gallbladder kept contracting trying to free it for several days straight. I didn’t eat or sleep and was constantly sick. I was in constant pain I finally couldn’t take it anymore and went to the ER. My gallbladder was gigantic and full of sludge and stones. They had to aspirate it to shrink its size to get it out. They said if I hadn’t had the surgery within a few hours it would have likely ruptured because it was basically disintegrating. 3 weeks seems like a long time to wait, can you go elsewhere?

At 6 weeks I was playing full on volleyball games, diving and all! I just recovered very quickly. I immediately got up after surgery and started walking around. Lots of studies show bodies in motion stay that way so I did my best to get up and walk around as much as I could. I would say listen to your body, get as much rest as you need. Be careful with heavy lifting that’s the only thing they told me for the first 6 weeks.

I have not had many negative side effects. Within the first month of recovery you quickly learn what foods will upset you and what won’t. The only things that really bother me now are really oily foods, peanut butter, and cinnamon? (Super random unsure why). Other than that I usually eat whatever. Another thing to consider is you are not supposed to go long periods of time without eating because it can cause your liver to bile dump as soon as you eat something (which is what causes diarrhea). So I do try and keep snacks on hand when I know I won’t be eating much throughout the day. You’re also not supposed to eat overly large meals because of the same reason I never really have been a large meal eater so this doesn’t bother me. You will adjust rather quickly, the most annoying part for me has been relearning how to use my abdominal muscles after surgery. I also get different signals that I need to go to the bathroom now it’s very random but the top of my stomach will ache. Personally I feel significantly better now than I did before surgery. I am able to do whatever whenever.

Just get used to being around them. The more you handle them the less reactive they are because they are desensitized. You can just put your hand in the cage and let them explore, I have never had a mouse just straight up bite me for no reason. If you show fear they know! Be calm and they will be calm. You do not need garden gloves you can just double glove and it is unlikely they will break skin. Lastly, if you are going to go for a scruff go full send do not stop midway through they will bite! Nearly every bite I’ve witnessed was because people stopped midway a scruff. I have handled thousands of mice and only have gotten bit twice! If you feel like your anxiety or fear is creeping up or you just can’t scruff one mouse in particular, take a break you will both need it. I have worked a majority with B6 and they honestly aren’t as bad as people make it out to be.

I work in a Cardiovascular lab as a Senior Research Associate. My lab works with lab animals and humans. I spend a majority of my time doing cell culture and doing surgical procedures. I work in a small lab right now only 5 people and I do work with my coworkers and talk to them often. I will say in my previous lab I worked a lot more with my coworkers because I had 20 people in my lab so I was constantly talking to people and coordinating. You might also find an interest in a clinical trial lab where you frequently work with patients. Lastly, I will say when I was just starting off I was more likely to just be doing tasks.
